title: UCM/ROCM: intercept HSA allocator with bistro
body:
The ROCm memory hook installed only ELF relocation (GOT) patches on hsa_amd_memory_pool_allocate/free. This PR introduces the bistro approach.

title: UCT/IB: Dump complete packets in trace-data logs
body:
## What?

`uct_ib_log_dump_sg_list()` copies the packet into a fixed `char data[256]` before handing it to the dump callback, which then parses past the end of the copy for any larger packet. That is an out-of-bounds read of the stack buffer, and it prints a bogus description. Only reachable with trace-data logging enabled (`UCX_LOG_LEVEL=data` or more verbose); nothing is wrong on the wire.

A 325-byte `WIREUP REQ`, before and after:

```
am 1 WIREUP REQ [<malformed address> uuid 0x0 src_ep_id 0x15554c607140 ...]
am 1 WIREUP REQ [funk03:1604837 uuid 0xd3a9b6897678a217 src_ep_id 0x15554c607140 ...] s...
```

## Why?

The dump callbacks parse a message by its own headers and get no length they can rely on — `ucp_address_unpack()` takes none at all — so a truncated copy makes them walk off its end. Only the send path was affected; receive completions pass the real buffer through.

## How?

Size the gather buffer to the message with `ucs_alloc_on_stack()`, so only large packets reach the heap. Skip the callback when nothing was collected, since it has no header to read. A description can still be cut by the log line length, so stamp the line end with an ellipsis; one that fits keeps its own terminator and hides the stamp. Verified on ConnectX with loopback `ucx_perftest` and the `rc_mlx5`/`ud_mlx5` p2p gtests under `UCX_LOG_LEVEL=data`.

title: UCP/PROTO: Fix buffer copy estimation for CPU-accessible memory
body:
## What?

`ucp_proto_init_add_buffer_copy_time()` modeled a plain memcpy only when both buffers are `UCS_MEMORY_TYPE_HOST`. For the other memory types in `UCS_MEMORY_TYPES_CPU_ACCESSIBLE` — ze-host, ze-managed and rocm-managed — this went wrong in two different ways:

- Direct-access protocols, which set `memtype_op == UCT_EP_OP_LAST`, fell through to the memtype endpoint lookup and returned `UCS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, so the candidate could be **rejected**. `ucp_proto_buffer_copy_factor_id()` also
  asserted that the operation is `GET_ZCOPY` or `PUT_ZCOPY`, which aborted:

   ```sh
   proto_init.c:292  Assertion `(memtype_op == UCT_EP_OP_GET_ZCOPY) || (memtype_op == UCT_EP_OP_PUT_ZCOPY)' failed: memtype_op=16
   ```

- Eager bcopy protocols, which set `UCT_EP_OP_GET_SHORT` or `UCT_EP_OP_PUT_SHORT`, were costed with the copy interface bandwidth, so the candidate was **mis-ranked**.

Neither matches runtime behavior: `ucp_dt_contig_pack()`/`unpack()` use memcpy for CPU-accessible memory and reach the memtype endpoint only for non-CPU-accessible memory.

Add `ucp_proto_buffer_copy_is_memcpy()` to decide when the copy is performed by the CPU, and use it for the memcpy estimation. Keep the explicit `UCT_EP_OP_LAST` branch in `ucp_proto_buffer_copy_factor_id()` so a contract violation reports both memory types instead of producing the misleading zero-copy-operation assertion.

## Why?

With `ze_copy`, initiating a 4 MB tag send from ze-host memory aborted while initializing protocol candidates. Even with the assertion silenced, the direct-access candidate was dropped, and the eager bcopy candidates were priced by the copy interface rather than by memcpy.

## How?

The predicate treats the copy as a memcpy for host/host, and for `UCT_EP_OP_LAST`, `UCT_EP_OP_GET_SHORT` and `UCT_EP_OP_PUT_SHORT` when both memory types are CPU accessible. `GET_ZCOPY`/`PUT_ZCOPY` keep the copy interface
estimation, because the rendezvous mtype protocols perform a real memtype endpoint copy.

This changes protocol selection, not only the abort. In the tested configuration, tag send from ze-host previously selected `eager short` at size 0 and rendezvous from one byte onward. It now selects:

```
      0..115  eager short
    116..404  eager copy-in copy-out
   405..8247  eager zero-copy copy-out
 8248..25731  multi-frag eager zero-copy copy-out
  25732..inf  rendezvous zero-copy read from remote
```

The crossover values are hardware dependent; the shape of the change is that eager is no longer priced out of small and mid-size messages.

Tests, in separate ZE and ROCm fixtures so an unsupported environment reports a skip rather than passing without assertions:

- `cpu_accessible_direct_proto_eligible` verifies `egr/short` is selected for each supported CPU-accessible memory type under `RNDV_THRESH=inf`. Reverting only the eligibility change reproduces the original assertion failure.
- `cpu_accessible_eager_costed_as_memcpy` verifies an eager protocol is selected at one byte with rendezvous enabled. Reverting only the SHORT handling makes it fail with `proto=tag/rndv`.
- `device_memory_uses_mtype_copy` verifies non-CPU-accessible memory still selects rendezvous, covering the CPU-accessible gate.

The ZE fixture covers ze-host and ze-managed; a separate fixture covers rocm-managed over `rc,rocm_copy`. This is protocol-selection coverage only; it does not exercise data movement.

Tested on Intel Arc Pro B60, `rc_mlx5` over RoCE:

- Protocol initialization completes. The thresholds above are observed for ze-host. ze-device is not CPU accessible and is unchanged.
- `ucx_perftest tag_lat -V` passes for ze-host and ze-managed, which aborted before.

Remaining gaps: CPU-accessible `GET_ZCOPY`/`PUT_ZCOPY` costing is not covered, because protocol selection reaches that path only above a hardware-dependent threshold and neither `RNDV_THRESH` nor `RNDV_SCHEME` reliably forces it for
these memory types; covering it would need a lower-level test that constructs and inspects buffer-copy performance directly with a configured memtype endpoint. The same SHORT reclassification applies to rocm-managed, but its protocol-selection impact was not validated on ROCm hardware.

title: UCS/RCACHE: Adds capability for merging adjacent rcache regions
body:
## Why?
Reduce the number of memory keys in use for sequences of adjacent memory regions. When using too many memory keys, NIC can run out of resources and fail to register memory.
Fixes #6264 

## What?
When enabled, rcache regions of adjacent memory will be merged. Merges only occur when new region is the same size or larger than the existing region. This prevents continually reregistering the same memory region when adding many small regions in a row.

## How?
The rcache already has handling for memory regions that overlap with existing registrations. This is extend to handle regions that sit adjacent in memory when enabled. This is a little more difficult. Overlapping regions can be can safely be assumed to be of the same memory type and from the same allocation. This isn't true for adjacent memory regions. This is handled by checking to make sure that the regions have the same memory type, memory flags, and are part of the same allocation.

title: UCT/IB/RC/VERBS: Support QPs without SRQ
body:
## What?
Enable rc_verbs on devices without SRQ by posting receive WRs to each QP.

Add configuration for selecting SRQ usage and setting the receive WR count per
QP. Update flow control, RX CQ accounting and QP cleanup for this mode.

Two pre-existing bugs are fixed as separate commits, because the new mode
reaches both of them. They change existing behavior of the SRQ path:

- An endpoint is added to iface->ep_list when uct_rc_ep_t is initialized, but
  it was removed outside of the uct_rc_ep_t cleanup, so an endpoint whose
  initialization failed was freed while still on the list. The removal is moved
  to the uct_rc_ep_t cleanup and dropped from rc_verbs, rc_mlx5 and gga_mlx5.
- A receive descriptor is taken from the interface pool for every receive WR
  posted to the SRQ, but a completion which reported an error skipped the
  release of the descriptor while the SRQ counted the WR as available, so every
  failed receive leaked one descriptor.

## Why?
rc_verbs currently requires every device to support SRQ during transport
discovery. Some devices, such as eRDMA, support RC QPs but do not support SRQ,
so rc_verbs is not exposed on them. Supporting QPs without SRQ enables a wider
range of RDMA devices to use UCX through rc_verbs.

## How?
- Add RC initialization attributes and a QP receive WR count.
- Select SRQ or per-QP receive posting during interface initialization.
- Track and refill receive WRs per endpoint.
- Limit the flow control window to the receive capacity of one QP.
- Defer QP destruction until its receive WR completions are drained, since
  IBV_EVENT_QP_LAST_WQE_REACHED is not generated for a QP without an SRQ.
- Refuse endpoint creation when the RX CQ has no room left for the receive WRs
  of one more QP, which makes max_num_eps an enforced limit.

The gtest coverage of this mode is a follow-up PR #11938.

title: UCP/RKEY: Keep configurations at stable addresses
body:
## What?

Store each rkey configuration separately from the resizable index array, and
update its users and tests for pointer-based storage.

This PR now contains only the stable-storage change. It depends on #11817 to
keep protocol selection out of async context; it does not add async locking.

## Why?

Protocol selection can recursively create another rkey configuration. With
inline storage, growing the array copies a partially initialized configuration
while the outer selection continues updating the old address. Later lookups
then use an incomplete copy.

This is reachable without an injected configuration: on Gaia, normal
default-reserve traffic naturally moved the array from 32 to 64 while an outer
rkey configuration was live. A diagnostic consistency check observed
`put_short` diverging between the old and current copies in 4/5 runs.

## How?

The resizable array stores pointers to separately allocated configurations.
Growing the array can move the pointer slots, but it cannot move a live
configuration. Worker cleanup destroys and frees each configuration.

## Validation

- Rebased onto current `master` and updated all current-master rkey-config
  test accesses.
- Exact #11817: 20/20 ordinary runs completed; the observation-only natural
  relocation check detected stale/current state divergence in 4/5 runs.
- Current `master` + #11817 + this PR: clean build, 31/31 selected tests,
  20/20 natural two-node runs, and 5/5 forced 32-to-33 pointer-array
  relocations. Every forced marker reported synchronous context.

title: UCP/PROTO: Apply GPU-NIC assignment to RMA and rendezvous lanes
body:
## What?
Restrict the RMA_BW lanes of zcopy RMA and rendezvous protocols to the NICs assigned to the GPU that owns the buffer.

## How?
- The owner is the staging buffer's GPU for pipeline (mtype) protocols when it is known, otherwise the application buffer's GPU. Non-CUDA memory and GPUs without an assignment keep the existing lane selection logic.
- Unassigned RMA_BW lanes are removed before lane performance is queried. If none are left, the protocol is skipped.
- The assignment applies to put/get zcopy (including IOV and SGL) and to rendezvous get/put, both zcopy and mtype. Bcopy is excluded, because with CUDA memory it only handles zero-length messages.
- When an assignment is in use, ties between equally fast lanes always go to the first lane, `SINGLE_NET_DEVICE` filtering is skipped.
- Tests use a mocked `rc_mlx5` fixture with a synthetic assignment.

title: UCP/DEVICE: Retry remote mem list create on wireup lane
body:
## What?
Return `UCS_ERR_NOT_CONNECTED` instead of `UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE` from `ucp_device_remote_mem_list_create()` when a device lane is still a wireup proxy.

## Why?
Real life issue also seen as intermittent CI failure:

```
[ RUN      ] rc_gda/test_ucp_device.get_remote_mem_list_length/1 <rc,rc_gda,cuda_copy,rocm_copy/cuda>
ucp_device.c:553  UCX  ERROR failed to get device_ep for lane=2
ucp_device.c:818  UCX  ERROR failed to create handle: No resources are available to initiate the operation
test/gtest/ucp/test_ucp_device.cc:219: Failure
Error: No resources are available to initiate the operation
[  FAILED  ] rc_gda/test_ucp_device.get_remote_mem_list_length/1
```

`ucp_wireup_remote_connected()` sets `UCP_EP_FLAG_REMOTE_CONNECTED` but only schedules `ucp_wireup_eps_progress()` to install the real transport endpoints. Until it runs, the lane is a `ucp_wireup_ep_t` whose stub iface returns `UCS_ERR_NO_RESOURCE`, so callers retrying on `UCS_ERR_NOT_CONNECTED` get a hard error. `ucp_device_remote_mem_list_params_check()` does not cover this window.

## How?
Test `ucp_wireup_ep_test()` on the lane in `ucp_device_remote_mem_list_element_pack()` and return `UCS_ERR_NOT_CONNECTED`, which is already retryable and not error-logged. The existing `err:` path frees elements packed so far, so retries do not leak. Only the device lane is checked, since the CM lane keeps its wireup endpoint permanently.

## Verification
Built with `--with-gda`; `rc_gda/test_ucp_device.*` and `cuda_ipc/test_ucp_device.*` pass (20 tests).

The race does not reproduce by looping (25 runs passed): the scheduled callback usually runs within the same `ucp_worker_progress()` call. Temporarily patching `ucp_wireup_eps_progress()` to defer itself once reproduced the CI log exactly and confirmed `REMOTE_CONNECTED` was already set; with the fix the errors disappear. That instrumentation is not part of this PR.

title: UCT/IB: Add refcounted, TTL-based address handle cache
body:
## What?

- AH cache holds a refcnt to each entry; evict (release refcnt and re-query) on TTL expiration, regardless of refcnt.
- Only `ud_v` and `srd` hold a long-term AH reference. The transports (`rc_x`, `ud_x`, `dc`) release any reference right away as they mainly need an AV for connect.
- `ud_v` and `srd` functions `is_connected()`/ conn_match: compare peer identity (dlid/gid), not AH pointer value.

Important: TTL=0 means full cache bypass, no refcnt.

## Why?

The AH cache had no lifecycle, entries were never re-resolved or reclaimed, and `is_connected()` relied on that by comparing AH pointers directly. Adding refcnt/TTL-based eviction makes pointer comparison unsafe for TTL=0, so identity-based comparison is needed too.

Cache use-case: quickly reconnecting endpoints speedup.

title: TOOLS/PERF: swap deprecated omp pragma master to masked
body:
## What?
This PR swaps `#pragma omp master` to `#pragma omp masked` in `perftest.c` in order to better align with OpenMP version 5.1 and above.

## Why?
As of OpenMP 5.1, the 'master' construct has been deprecated in favor of 'masked'. As per the OpenMP specification:

> The directive-name `master` may be used as a synonym to `masked` if no clauses are speciﬁed. This syntax has been deprecated.

https://www.openmp.org/spec-html/5.2/openmpse61.html

This causes a warning under GCC 16, which is made into a build failure by -Werror.

This closes #11061. See that issue for an example error, which I've reproduced with GCC version 16.1.0 on x86_64-linux.

## How?
On OpenMP versions which support it (5.1, or `202011`), this changes to using `#pragma omp masked` while conditionally leaving `#pragma omp master` on older versions.

I apologize for any procedural mistakes here, trying to figure out how these CI systems work as I go.

title: TOOLS/PERF: Replace deprecated omp master pragma with masked
body:
## What

`ucx_perftest` fails to build with GCC 16: the OpenMP `master` construct is deprecated since OpenMP 5.1, and `BASE_CFLAGS` carries `-Werror`.

```
perftest.c:251:11: error: 'master' construct deprecated since OpenMP 5.1, use 'masked' [-Werror=deprecated-openmp]
perftest.c:585:9:  error: 'master' construct deprecated since OpenMP 5.1, use 'masked' [-Werror=deprecated-openmp]
```

Fixes #11061.

## How

Use `masked` when `_OPENMP >= 202011`, keep `master` otherwise. `masked` without a `filter` clause is semantically identical to `master`. Both sites are converted, including `mpi_rte_barrier()` under `HAVE_MPI`.

The guard is required: GCC 11-13 report `_OPENMP=201511` and would warn `-Wunknown-pragmas` on a bare `masked`. GCC 16.2.1 reports `202111`.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
docker run --mount type=bind,src=$(pwd),dst=/ucx -it fedora:rawhide bash
```

```bash
dnf -y install autoconf automake libtool make gcc gcc-c++ git file openmpi-devel
export PATH=/usr/lib64/openmpi/bin:$PATH   # before configure: mpi.m4 probes mpicc/mpirun
cd /ucx && ./autogen.sh
./contrib/configure-devel --with-mpi
grep 'define HAVE_MPI' config.h
make -j          # or: make -C src/tools/perf ucx_perftest-perftest.o
```

Parent commit reproduces both errors; with this commit it builds clean with and without `--with-mpi`.

title: UCP/RNDV: Throttle rndv fragment requests
body:
## What?
Added a worker-level throttling mechanism for rndv fragment requests (both pipeline and standalone mtype requests).

## Why?
Without throttling, rendezvous protocols can spawn an unbounded number of concurrent fragment requests, each allocating staging memory from GPU memory pools. Under heavy workloads, this leads to GPU memory exhaustion (OOM), as tracked in https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/5359018. The throttling mechanism bounds the number of in-flight fragments per worker, preventing resource exhaustion while allowing work to progress as fragments complete.

## How?
The throttling is implemented using a worker-level flow control state (`worker->rndv_ppln_fc`) consisting of:
- An `active_frags` counter tracking currently in-flight fragment operations
- A `pending_q` queue holding throttled requests waiting for resources

When a new fragment request would exceed `UCX_RNDV_PPLN_WORKER_MAX_FRAGS`, the request is queued in `pending_q`. When fragments complete, `active_frags` is decremented and one queued request is rescheduled via `ucs_callbackq_add_oneshot()` to the main progress loop.

The mechanism applies to:
- Pipeline fragment dispatch in `rndv_ppln.c`
- Standalone `mtype` protocols in `rndv_rtr.c`, `rndv_get.c`, and `rndv_put.c`.

title: UCS/DATASTRUCT: Add interval map
body:
## What?
Add ucs_interval_map_t, a map of half-open intervals to caller-owned objects. Unlike ucs_interval_tree_t, which coalesces, it keeps overlapping intervals distinct: inserting [0,4) and [2,6) yields two entries, both findable.

It is a ucs_rbtree_t ordered by interval start and augmented with each subtree's maximum end, so finding an interval that contains a given range costs O(log n). Nodes are intrusive and caller-allocated, and removal never relocates one, so removal by a held pointer needs no search.

## Why?
Usable as a cache for regions of vmm backed by multiple allocations in a future cuda_ipc change.

## How?
Reusing the rbtree struct, adding an augment function pointer to maintain the max end in the subtree.

title: UCT/CUDA: Reject IPC without P2P read/write support
body:
## What?

Prevent CUDA IPC from being selected when NVML explicitly reports that the local and remote GPU pair does not support P2P read or write access.

CUDA IPC rkey unpack now resolves the local and remote GPU UUIDs through NVML and marks the rkey unreachable when either P2P capability is unsupported. UCP also excludes unreachable memory domains when modeling the nested rendezvous protocol, allowing the existing host-staged pipeline to be selected.

NVML lookup failures and unknown P2P status retain the existing IPC handle mapping probe as a fallback. A focused multi-GPU regression test compares the NVML result with `cuDeviceCanAccessPeer()` across the locally visible devices.

## Why?

Successfully importing a CUDA IPC handle does not guarantee that the GPU pair supports P2P read and write access. On an AWS `g7e.48xlarge` containing 8 x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, CUDA permits mapping
memory between GPUs connected through different PCIe bridges even though NVML reports P2P access as unsupported. Transfers through that mapping are extremely slow.

Consequently, enabling `cuda_ipc` prevented UCX from selecting its faster host-staged pipeline and required users to explicitly disable the transport.

The system has eight GPUs arranged as four same-bridge pairs:

- `GPU0-GPU1`, `GPU2-GPU3`, `GPU4-GPU5`, and `GPU6-GPU7`: `PIX`
- GPU pairs behind different PCIe bridges in the same NUMA node: `NODE`
- GPU pairs across NUMA nodes: `SYS`

NVML reports read, write, and PCIe P2P support for the `PIX` pairs and `NVML_P2P_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` for the tested `NODE` and `SYS` pairs. The capability matrix was reproduced on a second identical `g7e.48xlarge`.

For example:

- `GPU0-GPU1`: `PIX`, P2P read/write supported
- `GPU0-GPU2`: `NODE`, P2P read/write unsupported

Results for 100 MiB messages with SRD disabled and `-O 2`:

| GPU pair | Topology | Unpatched | Patched | Selected data path |
|----------|----------|-----------|---------|--------------------|
| GPU0 -> GPU2 | `NODE`, P2P unsupported | 0.88 GB/s | 32.42 GB/s | `cuda_copy`/CMA host-staged pipeline |
| GPU0 -> GPU1 | `PIX`, P2P supported | N/A | 52.45 GB/s | CUDA IPC |

The cross-bridge result used `UCX_TLS=^srd`, so `cuda_ipc` remained enabled and was rejected automatically only for the unsupported GPU pair.

## How?

The packed CUDA IPC rkey already contains the remote GPU UUID. During rkey unpack, UCX now:

1. Resolves the local and remote UUIDs to NVML devices.
2. Queries P2P read and write capability.
3. Keeps CUDA IPC when both capabilities are supported.
4. Returns `UCS_ERR_UNREACHABLE` when either capability is explicitly unsupported.
5. Falls back to the existing handle-mapping probe when NVML cannot resolve the peer or reports an unknown result.

The unreachable CUDA IPC memory domain is then removed from the synthetic remote rkey used for nested rendezvous protocol selection. This preserves the local staging registration map while preventing the rejected CUDA IPC lane from
being selected again.

This is intentionally a conservative capability check rather than a bandwidth heuristic. GPU pairs for which NVML reports P2P read and write support remain eligible for CUDA IPC.

title: UCP/RMA: Make put/rndv and get/rndv a fallback of zcopy
body:
## What?
Make `get/zcopy` and `put/offload/zcopy` override `get/rndv` and `put/rndv`, which become their fallback, and remove `UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE`.

## Why?
- The RMA rendezvous protocols add an RTS/RTR round trip, and are only useful as a fallback where no direct zcopy path exists. This was approximated by a `UCS_CPU_MODEL_NVIDIA_VERA` gate, which made selection platform dependent.

## How?
- Add a fallback rule to protocol selection: a protocol declares the classes it belongs to in `proto_class`, and the classes it overrides in `fallback_class`. A protocol is dropped on message size ranges where another protocol declares its class as a fallback. Two new `ucp_proto_t` fields, both default 0, so other protocols are unaffected.
- `ucp_proto_select_disable_fallback()` runs per message size range in `ucp_proto_thresholds_next_range()`, so the rendezvous protocols stay available wherever zcopy has no range.
- It runs after the `cfg_thresh` and `cfg_priority` filters, so `UCX_ZCOPY_THRESH` is still honored: a zcopy protocol disabled below the configured threshold does not override its fallback.
- Classes are matched within a single selection key, which has one operation, so the put and get protocols share the `RMA_RNDV` class without affecting each other.
- Gtests with a synthetic class, and with a mock slow `GET_ZCOPY` device.

title: UCP/WIREUP: Activate AM lane iface while EP config is used
body:
## What?

Fix post wireup freeze by activating the interface of the AM lane during wireup, by adding that lane to the protocol lane map of the endpoint configuration.

Valid workaround: `UCX_ADAPTIVE_PROGRESS=n` as it otherwise deactivate interface in `ucp_worker_iface_init()`.

`UCX_LOG_LEVEL=data` triggers it because it sets `progress_wrapper_enabled` which disables short proto init that otherwise activate AM lane.

Non reduced repro:
```
env -u UCX_NET_DEVICES UCX_LOG_LEVEL=data \
    UCX_PROTO_INFO=used UCX_TLS=^gdr_copy \
    UCX_PROTOS=^get/rndv,put/rndv \
        ucx_perftest -t ucp_put_bw -m cuda -n 10`
```

## Why?

- The wireup ACK is sent on the AM lane, so its interface has to be progressed during wireup, before any data operation is issued.
- Today nothing progresses it at that point: the sender never reaps the ACK send completion, the peer never dispatches it, and both hang in a worker flush.
- It usually goes unnoticed because the interface is armed for events and something else wakes it up, or another endpoint or lane on the same interface has already activated it. Setups with several devices, where the AM lane sits on an interface nothing else uses, hit it.

## How?

- `ucp_ep_config_init()` seeds `proto_lane_map` with `key.am_lane`, so the interface is activated with the first endpoint using the configuration and released with the last one.
- `ucp_proto_select_elem_progress_ifaces()` already masks out the lanes of that map, so a protocol later selecting the AM lane does not activate it twice.
- Activating it from `ucp_wireup_should_activate_wiface()` instead would never be released, because `ucp_ep_unprogress_uct_ep()` is a no-op there.
- An interface which received messages is no longer kept activated once its last endpoint is destroyed: the counting proxy handler that used to activate it only runs while the interface is not activated, and that activation was never released. `test_ucp_sockaddr_iface_activate.iface_activate_count` is updated accordingly and still fails without the fix.
- New `test_ucp_wireup_1sided.am_lane_iface_activation` verifies the AM lane interface is activated after wireup, before any data operation.

title: UCP/FLUSH: Add topology-safe selective endpoint flush
body:
## What

Add an internal endpoint-flush primitive that can flush a selected lane mask, while preserving the current all-lanes endpoint-flush behavior for existing callers.

## Why

This is Part 1 of 5 of an updated split of the earlier [endpoint-fence PR #11199](https://github.com/openucx/ucx/pull/11199). Non-blocking endpoint fences need to identify precisely which lanes carry work that precedes a fence. Existing endpoint flushes must also remain safe when lane identities change during reconfiguration or failover.

This PR is useful independently: its existing callers still flush all lanes, but their flush state is now safely reconciled when a lane disappears or is replaced.

## How

- Add a selected-lane internal flush API; keep the public/all-lanes path as a wrapper over it.
- Track lane identity changes with an endpoint lane generation and reconcile a running flush with the current live lane map.
- Conservatively revisit current live lanes when the topology changed, so a stale lane index cannot make the flush miss work.
- Cover empty masks, lane replacement, lane generation, and reused lane-storage initialization.

title: UCP/PROTO: Reload proto_select after nested config allocation
body:
## What?

Nested protocol selection can reallocate worker config arrays and then use a stale `proto_select` / `rkey_config` pointer (UAF). Reload those pointers from the config indexes after the nested call returns.

## Why?

`worker->rkey_config` and `worker->ep_config` are growable worker arrays (not `ucp_ep_t`). Nested RTS probe can append an rkey config (`ucp_worker_add_rkey_config()`), realloc `worker->rkey_config[]`, and delayed-free the old buffer while `ucp_proto_select_lookup_slow` still holds `&rkey_config->proto_select`. The heap khash survives but the wrapper does not, so `proto_select->hash` can read as `NULL`.

This crash is the rkey array. The outer lookup uses `&ep_config->proto_select` in `worker->ep_config[]`, which is not grown here. The same realloc path exists for `ep_config[]` if a nested call adds an endpoint config.

```
ucp_proto_select_short_init
  ucp_proto_select_lookup_slow              /* outer: &ep_config->proto_select */
    ucp_proto_select_elem_init
      ucp_proto_select_init_protocols
        ucp_proto_rndv_rts_probe
          ucp_proto_rndv_ctrl_probe
            ucp_proto_rndv_ctrl_select_remote_proto
              rkey_config = &ucs_array_elem(...)   /* pointer taken */
              ucp_proto_select_lookup_slow         /* inner: &rkey_config->proto_select */
                kh_get(proto_select->hash)         /* still valid */
                ucp_proto_select_elem_init
                  /* add_rkey_config → worker->rkey_config[] realloc */
                kh_get(proto_select->hash)         /* UAF, hash == NULL */
```

## How?

Re-fetch `proto_select` (and other pointers into those arrays) after functions that can grow/realloc the worker config arrays.

title: ARCH/X86: Add AVX512 nt-buffer-transfer functions
body:
## What?

Add AVX512BW non-temporal destination and source kernels with masked edge handling. Select the AVX-512 implementation at compile time when `__AVX512BW__` is defined and retain AVX2 as the fallback.

This is the third part of the split from #11696, following #11878 and #11895.

## Why?

Use the full AVX-512 vector width for large cache-bypassing transfers and use byte masks for non-cache-line-aligned edges.

## How?

The NT destination kernel copies forward with streaming stores and an `sfence`. The NT source kernel copies backward with regular stores and no fence. Both implementations retain the existing dispatcher contract.

Build
AVX2: configure with --enable-optimizations.
AVX-512: add -march=znver5 or another target flag defining AVX512BW into CFLAGS.

Runtime requirements
Currently recommended for workloads using one MPI rank per L3 cache domain.

Required runtime arguments(config params):
UCX_NT_BUFFER_TRANSFER_MIN=0

The default UCX_NT_BUFFER_TRANSFER_MIN start threshold is three-quarters of the detected L3 cache size.

title: UCT/CUDA/COPY: Qualify cuda_copy for RNDV with peer-failure EH
body:
## What?

Allow same-UUID endpoints using `UCP_ERR_HANDLING_MODE_PEER` to select transports that do not support peer-failure handling or RMA invalidation, such as `cuda_copy`.

Changes:

1. `ucp_ep_err_mode_init_flags()` omits `UCP_EP_INIT_ERR_MODE_PEER_FAILURE` for same-UUID endpoints in `PEER`
   mode.
2. Wireup applies these effective flags only for lane selection, while the endpoint configuration retains `UCP_ERR_HANDLING_MODE_PEER`.
3. Recovery auxiliary transport selection uses the same effective flags.
4. Same-process endpoint configurations skip RMA-key invalidation, since their RMA-BW lanes may not support `UCT_MD_FLAG_INVALIDATE_RMA`.
5. Tests cover same-process peer-error wireup and optional RMA invalidation.

`UCP_ERR_HANDLING_MODE_FAILOVER` intentionally retains its full peer-failure requirements.

## Why?

With peer error handling and rendezvous enabled, wireup normally requires `UCT_IFACE_FLAG_ERRHANDLE_PEER_FAILURE` and `UCT_MD_FLAG_INVALIDATE_RMA`. `cuda_copy` does not provide these capabilities, so it cannot be selected as an RMA-BW lane even when the remote address has the same UUID as the local worker.

For same-UUID endpoints, there is no independent remote process whose failure requires cross-process RMA-key invalidation. Relaxing these transport-selection requirements allows the local copy path to be selected while preserving the
endpoint's requested `PEER` error-handling mode.

`FAILOVER` is not relaxed: its PSN-based recovery protocols require the full peer-failure behavior.

Cross-UUID endpoints are unchanged and retain the existing peer-failure and RMA-invalidation requirements.

Closes #11318

title: UCT/IB/MLX5: Purge outstanding AM short operations
body:
## What?
Add native RC mlx5 outstanding-operation purge support for active messages posted with `uct_ep_am_short()`.

The purge path:
- walks outstanding SEND WQEs in posting order
- uses the existing cumulative PSN tracking to distinguish delivered from undelivered packets
- reconstructs AM short operations for the callback
- skips internal NOP and flow-control-only WQEs
- rejects unsupported WQE layouts before invoking callbacks

## Why?
Fault-tolerance recovery needs the transport to report AM short operations that were not delivered after an endpoint is invalidated. RC mlx5 currently lacks native purge support for this operation.

This replaces the narrowly scoped UCT purge work from #11785.

## How?
Parse the outstanding send queue without adding send-time PSN bookkeeping. First validate the outstanding WQE range and derive packet PSNs from the existing `next_wqe_psn`, then report undelivered AM short operations through the UCT purge callback.

title: UCP: Split an SGL put between the lanes by bytes
body:
## What?
Count the SGL iterator length and offset in bytes, and give every lane an equal share of the message, splitting elements where a share ends.

## Why?

## How?

title: UCT/TCP: Stop writing PUT data of a canceled EP, report RMA invalidation
body:
Closes #11929

## What?

1. `uct_ep_flush(UCT_FLUSH_FLAG_CANCEL)` on a TCP EP now also stops PUT data which arrives from the peer from being written. The connection is closed, so nothing lands and the peer's PUT and flush complete with `UCS_ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`.
2. TCP MD reports `UCT_MD_FLAG_INVALIDATE_RMA`.

`uct_ep_destroy()` is not changed: an EP which is destroyed without being canceled keeps receiving, which the disconnect flows rely on.

## Why?

1. Cancel means the user gives up on the operations of the EP and may free or reuse their memory. On RDMA the QP is moved to the error state, so data which the peer is still writing does not land and the peer's operation fails. On TCP the cancel only purged the local operations, so a PUT which was in flight kept being written to the address from the PUT header, into memory the user already reused. We hit this in production: after a request was aborted and its buffer handed to another request, a 4MB PUT landed in it.

   UCP issues this cancel when an endpoint is closed with `UCP_EP_CLOSE_FLAG_FORCE` and when it discards the lanes of a failed endpoint (`ucp_ep_close_nbx`, `ucp_worker_discard_uct_ep`), which are exactly the paths after which the buffer is reused.

2. With `UCP_ERR_HANDLING_MODE_PEER` and rendezvous enabled, `ucp_wireup_add_rma_bw_lanes()` requires `UCT_MD_FLAG_INVALIDATE_RMA` from the MD. TCP MD did not report it, so `ucp_put` over TCP ran the AM based emulation (8KB fragments, a completion message each) instead of `put_zcopy`:

   | ucx_perftest -t ucp_put_bw -s 4M, tcp/lo | MB/s |
   |---|---|
   | without error handling (put_zcopy) | 11935 |
   | `-epeer` (AM emulation) | 2211 |

   On our TCP hosts the receiving CPU stayed at 100% in `ucp_put_handler` / `ucp_rma_sw_send_cmpl` and a connection was limited to 0.3-0.6 GB/s, against over 2 GB/s with put_zcopy.

   TCP MD registers no memory, so there is nothing to invalidate; what the flag has to guarantee, that a canceled operation does not land in memory the user reused and that the peer learns, is provided by the first commit. TCP has no atomics, so `UCT_MD_FLAG_INVALIDATE_AMO` is not reported, and with it not `UCT_MD_FLAG_INVALIDATE`, which means both.

## How?

`UCT_TCP_EP_FLAG_CANCELED` is set in `uct_tcp_ep_flush()`. `uct_tcp_ep_progress_am_rx()` closes the connection when a PUT request arrives on such an EP, and `uct_tcp_ep_progress_put_rx()` does the same for the rest of a PUT which was already in progress. AM is unaffected.

## Tests

`GTEST/UCT/TCP: Add a PUT after cancel test` - a 64MB PUT, so it spans many RX segments and is also received by `uct_tcp_ep_progress_put_rx()`. The receiver cancels its EP while the PUT is being received. Without the first commit the rest of the PUT is written into the canceled EP's buffer and the sender completes with success; with it nothing is written after the cancel and the sender gets `UCS_ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`.

`test_ucp_peer_failure_rndv_abort.put_zcopy_memory_invalidation` and `put_zcopy_force_flush_memory_invalidation` skipped on TCP until now ("transport has no rma_bw lanes"); they run and pass with this series.

`test_invalidate_rma_bw_lane()` expected a TCP RMA BW lane without invalidation support when rendezvous is disabled, and is updated.

Two UCP fixes are needed once TCP is used as an RMA BW lane. Both problems exist on master before this series and can be reproduced there by making TCP an RMA BW lane with `UCX_RNDV_THRESH=inf`:

- `ucp_request_get_invalidation_map()` asserted that every non p2p RMA BW lane supports get_zcopy, while such a lane can be put_zcopy only. This is what fails in `tcp/test_ucp_peer_failure_rndv_abort` on the IB workers.
- In `UCP_ERR_HANDLING_MODE_FAILOVER` only protocols which report `UCP_PROTO_COMMON_INIT_FLAG_FAILOVER` are selected, and the AM based GET emulation does not report it, so a transport without get_zcopy and get_bcopy has no GET protocol at all. `tcp/test_ucp_fault_tolerance` fails on all its GET variants without this.

Full gtest on x86_64, clean build of this series: 16123 passed, 1 failed - `malloc_hook_cplusplus.new_delete`, which fails the same way on master on this machine.

title: UCP/PROTO/RNDV: Isolate remote system device namespace
body:
## What?

Fix UCP rendezvous protocol selection for Direct NIC when system-device IDs
belong to different topology namespaces. Model GET/PUT mtype network lanes
using the staging fragment device.

## Why?

Direct NIC RNDV can fail in `find_lanes`: while estimating the protocol the
peer will select, UCX interprets a peer-local `sys_dev` from the rkey in the
local topology and can reject a valid lane. This remote-namespace correction
applies to both mtype and non-mtype protocols. For mtype GET/PUT, network I/O
accesses the staging fragment (for example, a host bounce buffer for CUDA),
but protocol selection still needs the user buffer `sys_dev` for lane
spreading.

## How?

Never interpret the rkey's peer-local `sys_dev` in the local topology. For
nested remote estimation, use the local `select_param.sys_dev` as a
namespace-safe topology proxy when the local and remote memory types match;
otherwise use `UCS_SYS_DEVICE_ID_UNKNOWN`. For mtype probes, keep the
user/final device in `select_param.sys_dev` and pass the staging fragment
through `reg_mem_info`. The common minimum-fragment filter validates
transport reachability once against `reg_mem_info`: for `SEND_ZCOPY` this
describes the selected user buffer, while RNDV mtype protocols supply their
staging fragment.

Keep the existing GPU peer-failure pipeline test deterministic by using a host
staging fragment; it still exercises CUDA user memory through
`rndv/put/mtype` and retains the original failure assertions. Regression
tests independently cover remote namespace isolation and the user/fragment
device roles.

title: UCT/CUDA_COPY: Skip dmabuf probe for async managed memory
body:
## What?
Fix CUDA async managed mempool memory detection in `cuda_copy` and add a regression test.

CUDA async managed allocations can report `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_IS_MANAGED` with no owning CUDA context. UCX now marks that case as async-managed, so `mem_flags` detection treats the memory as non-registerable and does not probe dmabuf export for it.

## Why?
With `UCX_CUDA_COPY_DMABUF=try`, posting a UCP receive into CUDA 13 async managed mempool memory can crash inside `cuMemGetHandleForAddressRange()`. Setting `UCX_CUDA_COPY_DMABUF=no` avoids the crash because UCX skips the dmabuf export probe.

The crash happens during UCP memory detection when `cuda_copy` queries `MEM_FLAGS`: the allocation is managed memory, but because it has no CUDA context, it must be handled like other async managed allocations and kept off the dmabuf/registration path.

## How?
The fix is local to `cuda_copy` memory attribute detection. When `cuPointerGetAttributes()` reports managed memory and the pointer has no CUDA context, mark it as `is_async_managed`. The existing mem_flags logic then returns non-registerable flags without calling `cuMemGetHandleForAddressRange()`.

A CUDA 13 regression test allocates async managed memory from the default managed mempool with `cudaMallocFromPoolAsync()`, queries `uct_md_mem_query_v2()` with `MEM_FLAGS` while `CUDA_COPY_DMABUF=try`, and verifies the memory is classified as `cuda-managed` and not registrable.

title: UCP/API: Endpoint parameter controlling remote key resources.
body:
## What?
Added a new UCP endpoint creation parameter. This parameter allows to manage the lifetime of resources used to work with a UCP remote key.
Added a new UCT remote key unpacking parameter. This parameter allows to manage the lifetime of resources used to work with the remote key.

## Why?
This is another attempt to solve the problem of unclosed interprocessor memory descriptors that prevent the memory from being released by the remote side.

https://github.com/openucx/ucx/pull/11335
https://github.com/openucx/ucx/pull/11288
https://github.com/openucx/ucx/pull/11730

At the moment the only way to close the handles is to disable UCT CUDA IPC remote cache. So behavior can only be controlled at the level of the whole process. The new parameters adds the possibility of more detailed control over the lifetime of objects.

title: UCT/CUDA_IPC: Support VMM with multiple memory allocations
body:
## What?
Add support for CUDA VMM allocations that span multiple underlying physical allocations (cuMemCreate chunks) in the cuda_ipc transport.

## Why?
A user-visible VA range may be backed by several independently created and mapped VMM chunks. Currently, cuda_ipc only exports a single fabric handle per region, which covers just the first chunk. This means transfers involving multi-chunk VMM regions silently access only the first chunk's memory, producing incorrect results for offsets beyond the first chunk boundary.

## How?
Introduce `UCT_CUDA_IPC_KEY_HANDLE_TYPE_VMM_MULTI`. During `mkey_pack`, cuda_ipc detects when the requested VMM range spans multiple allocation buffer IDs, discovers the chunks covering the expanded VA range, exports each chunk’s fabric handle, and writes the chunk descriptors into a GPU-resident metadata buffer. A small GPU-resident header points to that descriptor buffer, and the header fabric handle is packed in the rkey.
During `rkey_unpack`, the receiver imports the metadata header, performs a blocking DtoH copy of the header, imports the chunk-descriptor buffer, and performs another blocking DtoH copy to fetch all chunk handles. The VMM_MULTI memhandle open path then imports and maps the chunks into one contiguous local VA range, which is cached like other cuda_ipc mappings.

## Notes
1. Will be split into multiple PRs. This is just for completeness.
2. Posting performance is better than splitting the operation into one transfer per chunk, but worse than a single-allocation buffer because the resulting mapped range still has higher `cuMemcpyAsync` overhead.
3. A new cache is introduced for multi-allocation views, because now an allocation can map into multiple views but since the local buffer will be different these can't be merged

title: UCT/RC: Reserve TX credits for multi-credit sends
body:
## What?

Reserve the TX credits a multi-credit send needs, so that later single-credit sends on the same EP cannot consume them.

## Why?

`put_sgl_zcopy` needs `count` WQEs, so it returns `NO_RESOURCE` while credits are still available and is queued in pending. A later 1-credit AM then passes the resource check and is posted ahead of it:
```text
rc_iface.h:620 Assertion `iface->tx.in_pending || ucs_arbiter_group_is_empty(arb_group)' failed
```

## How?

Resource checks compare the available credits against `max(requirement, EP reservation)`, and a failing send records its requirement in `txqp_reserve` / `cq_reserve`. 
The reservation is released by `uct_rc_ep_schedule_pending()` once nothing is queued on the EP, and by `uct_rc_ep_pending_purge()`.

title: UCT/MM,BASE: Fail cleanly when an MM MD cannot provide a memory handle
body:
## What
Fail cleanly when an MM memory allocation does not produce a memory handle,
instead of dereferencing NULL later.

## Why
The POSIX MM MD re-evaluates `/dev/shm` on every `uct_md_query()` via `statvfs`.
If the free space drops below `UCX_POSIX_SHM_MIN_SIZE` after device enumeration
but before the iface is opened, the MD stops reporting `UCT_MD_FLAG_ALLOC`. The
receive FIFO is then allocated from the heap and `uct_iface_mem_alloc()` leaves
`memh` as `UCT_MEM_HANDLE_NULL`, which `uct_mm_iface_get_address()` dereferences
when it reads `seg->seg_id`. The result is a SIGSEGV at `MPI_Init` on nodes that
are temporarily low on shared memory.

The RX descriptor mpool has the same exposure later on. It grows lazily and each
chunk allocation re-queries the md, so a drop below the threshold after the iface
is open gives a chunk with a NULL memh, which `uct_mm_iface_recv_desc_init()`
dereferences when it reads `seg->length`.

## How
Check `recv_fifo_mem.memh` after the FIFO allocation and return
`UCS_ERR_NO_DEVICE`, and turn the existing debug-only assert in
`uct_iface_mp_chunk_alloc()` into a returned error.

The checks are deliberately not in `uct_iface_mem_alloc()`, since a NULL memh is
valid there for MDs that only need an rkey. gdr_copy and cuda_ipc rely on that
for host bounce buffers. `uct_iface_mpool_init()` is used only by mm, ib and
ugni, all of which dereference the handle.

Note the iface open failure is not silently absorbed: `UCS_ERR_NO_DEVICE`
propagates through `ucp_worker_iface_open()`, so `MPI_Init` fails with an error
rather than falling back to another transport. That is still preferable to a
crash.

A regression gtest clears `UCT_MD_FLAG_ALLOC` from the MD query, matching what
`uct_posix_md_query()` does when the file system runs low, and then opens an mm
iface. Without the fix the test segfaults.

title: UCP/WIREUP: Improve p2p lane matching diagnostics
body:
## What?
Improve wireup p2p lane matching diagnostics, and report an ep address overflow as a fatal error instead of a debug-only assertion.

Related: https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6665318
## Why?
When an endpoint selects more lanes toward a remote device than the peer packed ep addresses for, `ucp_wireup_match_p2p_lanes()` reads past `ep_addrs[]`: debug builds assert, release builds pick up a zeroed entry and die later with a message naming neither the local device nor the remote address entry. Diagnosing it required the peer's pack traces to learn which devices `addr[N]` and each lane referred to.
## How?
Ep address overflow, now fatal in release builds too:
```diff
- Assertion `ep_addr_index < address->num_ep_addrs' failed: lane=7/14 tl_name_csum=0xd47a address_index=3 ep_addr_index=2 num_ep_addrs=2
+ Fatal: ep 0xfffd7c000140: lane[7] rc_mlx5/mlx5_0:1.1 -> addr[3] rc_mlx5: no ep address 2, only 2 provided
```
Duplicate remote lane:
```diff
- Fatal: ep 0xfffd7c000140: remote lane 0 is used more than once
+ Fatal: ep 0xfffd7c000140: lane[7] rc_mlx5/mlx5_0:1.1 -> addr[3]: remote lane 0 is used more than once
```
Missing remote ep address in `ucp_wireup_connect_local()`:
```diff
- ep 0xfffd7c000140: no remote ep address for lane[2]->remote_lane[5]
+ ep 0xfffd7c000140: lane[2] rc_mlx5/mlx5_1:1.0: no remote ep address for remote lane 5
```
Lane construction trace, the only lane-to-device record when an unchanged config skips `ucp_wireup_print_config()`:
```diff
- ep 0xfffd7c000140: construct lane 7 to addr_index 3
+ ep 0xfffd7c000140: construct lane 7 rc_mlx5/mlx5_0:1.1 to addr_index 3
- ep 0xfffd7c000140: construct lane 0 to addr_index 4294967295
+ ep 0xfffd7c000140: construct lane 0 cm
```
Address unpack trace, so the receiver's log is self-describing:
```diff
- unpack addr[3] : sysdev 6 paths 2 eps 2 tl_flags 0x39a bw 45747.33/nMBs ...
```

## What?

Add six OSes to the Azure PR pipeline, both arches: Fedora 44, Ubuntu 26.10, Azure Linux 4.0 (preview), openEuler 22.03 SP4 and 24.03 SP3, UOS 20.1060a.

## Retired (second commit)

Agreed with UCX dev management once the new rows were green:

| row | reason |
|---|---|
| `rhel76` | RHEL 7 EOL 2024-06 |
| `debian109` | Debian 10 LTS ended 2024-06 |
| `ubuntu1804` | EOL 2023-05 |
| `ubuntu2004`, `ubuntu2004_rocm` | Ubuntu 20.04 EOL 2025-05 |
| `ubuntu2210` | interim, EOL 2023-07 |
| `fedora41` | EOL 2025-12, replaced by `fedora44` |
| `euleros2sp12` | DOCA 3.5 dropped EulerOS; the openEuler rows cover it |
| `kylin10sp3` | OFED now targets Kylin V11 only |

`debian113` (LTS ended 2026-08-31) drops to `sanity`; `centos7` stays as `sanity`. Containers for the retired rows go too. Two of them were used outside the build matrix: `Build_Static` built on Ubuntu 20.04 and 18.04 and now builds on 22.04 and 24.04, and `rhel76` was the unused default of the `coverity.yml` container parameter, now `coverity_rh7`. Same images removed from the Jenkins matrix.

Net Build stage: 51 -> 42 rows.

## Why?

No CI coverage on any of them. Fedora 41 is long EOL; openEuler is where the OFED trains are going (MLNX_OFED 26.07 dropped `openeuler22.03sp3` for sp4, DOCA 3.5 dropped EulerOS).

## How?

- `buildlib/pr/main.yml`: 12 containers, images on `rdmz-harbor` (all present).
- `buildlib/pr/build_job.yml`: 6 rows in the x86_64 matrix, 6 in aarch64. `sanity` for inbox-only rows, `short` for OFED-backed rows and aarch64, matching the existing split.
- `.ci/pipeline/build_matrix.yaml`: same 12 rows so the Jenkins matrix does not drift.
- openEuler is DOCA on x86_64, MOFED on aarch64 (DOCA has no aarch64 openEuler). UOS is DOCA on x86_64, inbox on aarch64.
- Images from Mellanox-lab/hpcx-build#233; merge that first. The `fedora44` rows need #11908 (GCC 16 vs `omp master`).
- Third commit is a temporary copy of #11908 (both GCC 16 fixes) so the `fedora44` rows can build here; drop it before merge.

## Not fixed here

- Fedora 44 ships GCC 16, which rejects `#pragma omp master` and three set-but-unused gtest counters under `-Werror`. Fixed in #11908; carried here as a temporary test commit until it lands.

title: CI: Run the DL cluster job on the GB200 partition
body:
## What?
Get `ucx-test-dl-gpu` running on the GB200 DL cluster.

## Why?
The job never passed: it timed out waiting for a node on `gb300nvl72_ci`, and even with a node one worker could not finish the suite in time.

## How?
- Partition `gb200nvl72_ci` / account `oberon-gb-ci` (99 nodes vs 36, tied together by the cluster's `cli_filter`).
- Four sharded allocations (`worker` axis), separate checkout and test steps, `make -j32`, 180-min test step.
- `dl-base` rebased on the CUDA 13 release image (`buildlib/dockers`) plus gdrcopy, so CUDA tests build and run; no local `useradd` needed.
- `try_load_cuda_env` only needs `nvidia_peermem` on Azure; dlcluster uses dmabuf.

## UCX issues surfaced (not fixed here)
GB200: aarch64, GPUDirect via dmabuf, no `nvidia_peermem`.
- Segfault when cuda-managed registration fails: `dcx/test_ucp_mmap.rndv_mpool_mdesc_no_rcache/2` (`ucp_mm.c:84` EIO -> `mpool.c:246` -> SIGSEGV). Same crash-after-failure pattern after `cuda_ipc/test_cuda_ipc_md.mkey_pack_mempool/0` and `dc_mlx5/uct_p2p_rma_test.{put_short,put_zcopy,get_bcopy}`.
- Hangs until timeout: `ucp_client_server -c stream -s 1` (intermittent, both fleets), `dcx/test_ucp_tag_mt.send_recv`.
- `test_ucp_devices_config_mlx5.range_negate*` assumes contiguous `mlx5_0..N`; nodes have `mlx5_6`, `mlx5_16`.
- `shm/test_ucp_wait_mem.envelope/0`: `ucp_worker_wait_mem()` ~40x slower than reference put on aarch64.
- `Endpoint timeout` over RoCE: `test_ucp_tag_nbx.fallback/2` (rc/rcx/dcx/shm_ib), `rcx/test_ucp_rma_mt.put_get/0`.
- Also failing: `rc_verbs/uct_p2p_rma_test_inlresp.get_*_inlresp*`, `all/test_ucp_ep_based_fence.test_ep_based_fence_get/0`.

Logs (internal link):
https://nbuprod.blsm.nvidia.com/nbu-swx-ucx-master/job/UCX-OSS/job/ucx-test-dl-gpu-oss/26/
